items.title: Kolmogorov analytic partial sum maximal function
items.statement: On T=R/Z with measure dx, for P=sum(k=0..d) a_k exp(2 pi i k x), put A_n P=sum(k=0..min(n,d)) a_k e_k and A_*^d P=max(0<=n<=d)|A_n P|. An analytic polynomial has no negative frequencies.
items.proof_plan: Finite sums are continuous. Their finite absolute maximum is continuous; coefficients are unique by integrating products of characters. This definition neither asserts a maximal inequality nor changes symmetric S_N.

items.title: Kolmogorov simultaneous phase approximation
items.statement: If 1,x_1,...,x_r are Q-linearly independent, then for any unimodular z_j and epsilon>0, some positive integer L has |e_L(x_j)-z_j|<epsilon for all j.
items.proof_plan: Proposed local proof: use a product of nonnegative continuous one-variable bumps supported in the prescribed arcs. Approximate each uniformly by Fejer polynomials and multiply; constant coefficient is the product of the positive integrals. Average each nonconstant character along m(x_1,...,x_r), m=1..M: geometric sums tend to zero by rational independence. Uniform approximation transfers the positive limiting average to the bump product, so one positive m hits all arcs. This avoids assuming multidimensional Fourier inversion.

references.title: Grafakos, Classical Fourier Analysis, third edition

items.title: Kolmogorov atomic kernel maxima
items.statement: Assume AC. For arbitrarily large n there are t_j in ((j-1)/n,j/n), with 1,t_1,...,t_n Q-independent, such that B_L(x)=n^(-1)sum_j D_L(x-t_j) has sup(L>=1)|B_L(x)|>=c log n almost everywhere, for an absolute c>0.
items.proof_plan: Choose each t_j outside the rational span of previous choices, using countability and positive interval measure. For x outside span_Q(1,t_1,...,t_n), the differences and 1 are independent. Apply the phase lemma with target i exp(-pi i(x-t_j)) sign(sin(pi(x-t_j))). Each sine numerator then has the sign of its denominator and magnitude >1/2. The near-uniform spacing bounds the reciprocal-distance sum below by c n log n, including the end intervals. Define B_L as a finite average, avoiding an unprovided general convolution-of-measures theorem. AC is a sufficient hypothesis for choosing the family used at subsequent stages; finite choice alone suffices for fixed n.

references.title: Grafakos, Classical Fourier Analysis, third edition

items.title: Kolmogorov block polynomial with large partial sums
items.statement: Assume AC. For each H>0 and 0<eta<1 there is an analytic polynomial P with ||P||_1=1 and m{A_*P>H}>1-eta. Also retain the stronger source interface: a nonnegative symmetric polynomial g, ||g||_1=1, with m{sup_N|S_N g|>H}>1-eta.
items.proof_plan: Choose n with c log n>4H+4. Continuity from below selects a finite maximal cutoff R outside an exceptional set <eta. Set g=n^(-1)sum_j F_M(x-t_j); positivity and integral one are exact. For fixed R, the Fejer multiplier 1-|k|/(M+1) makes all S_r g uniformly close to B_r, r<=R. For d=degree(g), put P=e_d g: its spectrum is [0,2d] and norm stays one. Identity S_r g=e_{-d}(A_{d+r}P-A_{d-r-1}P), with A_{-1}=0, shows max|A P|>=max|S g|/2. Preserve the nonnegative symmetric clause for the published recorded-result replacement; the analytic clause alone would not replace it.

items.title: Separated frequency blocks do not disturb earlier partial sum maxima
items.statement: Let P(x)=sum_{k=0}^d c_k exp(2 pi i k x), m>=1 and a a scalar. Put Q=a exp(2 pi i m x)P. Then Q has support in [m,m+d], A_N Q=0 for N<m, and A_{m+r}Q=a exp(2 pi i m x)A_r P for 0<=r<=d. Hence later separated blocks leave earlier cutoffs unchanged, and internal maxima scale by |a|. Completed magnitude is exactly |a||P|; any amplitude bound must be supplied separately. In particular, on any set E, |a| sup_E |P|<=epsilon implies sup_E |Q|<=epsilon. Frequency translation alone supplies no magnitude reduction.
items.proof_plan: The Fourier coefficient at m+k is a c_k and all others are zero. Substituting those coefficients into each finite partial sum gives the three identities, including zero sums before m. The exponential has modulus one, so both partial-sum and completed magnitudes multiply by |a|. For multiple disjoint blocks, any earlier cutoff is below every later support. The pointwise amplitude assertion follows from the same exact equality; P=1 proves that modulation alone cannot make a nonzero completed block small. This finite algebra statement makes no choice or convergence claim.

items.title: Kolmogorov gliding hump series converges in lone
items.statement: Assume AC. Choose analytic blocks P_j with norm one and large internal maxima, summable a_j>0, disjoint increasing positive frequency intervals for Q_j=a_j e_{m_j}P_j, and summable exceptional measures, so sum Q_j converges in L1(T).
items.proof_plan: Using the corrected SH coefficient identities, take a_j=2^(-j), heights j/a_j and eta_j=2^(-j). Use AC to select countably many block polynomials; choose m_j by least integers beyond previous supports. Sum ||Q_j||_1<=1; MCT on sum |Q_j| gives a finite a.e. dominating function and a complex integrable pointwise sum, with L1 tail <=sum_{k>j}a_k. Alternatively use the published complex completeness theorem, retaining its choice hypothesis. No Parseval is needed.

items.title: Kolmogorov block maxima diverge off a null limsup set
items.statement: Assume AC and the preceding block construction. Off a null set, the symmetric partial sums of its L1 limit are unbounded.
items.proof_plan: First prove coefficient identification: |hat(f-sum_{j<=J}Q_j)(k)|<=||f-sum Q_j||_1. Disjoint supports identify every coefficient and show later blocks vanish at a current internal cutoff. Earlier blocks contribute sum_{i<j}Q_i(x), bounded by sum_i|Q_i(x)|<infinity a.e. Borel-Cantelli for bad block sets gives internal maxima >=j eventually. Thus |S_{m_j+r_j} f|>=j-sum_i|Q_i| tends to infinity along cutoffs. All frequencies of f are nonnegative, so the one-sided cutoffs equal symmetric ones.

items.statement: If m(E_j)<=2^(-j) for j>=1, then m(limsup E_j)=0.
items.proof_plan: The geometric sum is one; apply the measure version of Borel-Cantelli. Independence is unnecessary. For a direct check m(union_{j>=J}E_j)<=2^(1-J), hence the limsup has measure zero.

items.title: Carleson operator and measurable linearisation
items.statement: Assume AC for the Schwartz transform and integrability suppliers. For Schwartz f on R with hat f(xi)=integral f(x)e^(-2 pi i x xi)dx, set C_R f(x)=sup_a |integral_{-infinity}^a hat f(xi)e^(2 pi i x xi) dxi|. A finite rational cutoff maximum is linearised by a measurable selector a(x), with a measurable unimodular testing phase when dualising.
items.proof_plan: Continuity in cutoff makes the rational supremum equal to the full supremum for Schwartz input. Enumerate rationals, break finite-maximizer ties by least index; selector sets are Borel since the integrals are continuous. Extend beyond Schwartz only after uniform estimates. Include the phase when converting an absolute pairing estimate into a positive test.

items.title: Carleson tiles wave packets and tile order
items.statement: Assume AC for the Fourier suppliers. A tile s=I_s x omega_s consists of half-open dyadic intervals with |I_s||omega_s|=1. Write omega_s- and omega_s+ for its halves. For fixed Schwartz phi with smooth Fourier support strictly inside a small neighborhood of zero, set phi_s=Mod_{c(omega_s-)} Tr_{c(I_s)} Dil^2_{|I_s|} phi. Set s<=t when I_s subset I_t and omega_t subset omega_s. A tree lies below a designated top. Fix a nonzero packet by requiring 1 on [-1/9,1/9] and smooth Fourier support in [-1/8,1/8]; supply its construction locally.
items.proof_plan: Choose a nonzero smooth compactly supported Fourier bump and obtain phi by Schwartz inversion. L2 normalization uses |I|^(-1/2); frequency support lies in the lower half. Inclusion proves reflexivity, antisymmetry and transitivity. Define +trees by upper halves containing the top frequency and -trees by lower halves. No claim that arbitrary packets are orthogonal. The flat function is proved locally by the polynomial recurrence P_0=1, P_{k+1}=u^2(P_k-P_k prime), exponential domination for continuity and the difference quotient at zero. No B-page flat-function result is used.

items.title: Density size and tree count for carleson tiles
items.statement: Assume AC for the packet suppliers. For finite S, testing set E and selector N, define chi_I(x)=|I|^(-1)(1+|x-c(I)|/|I|)^(-kappa), kappa large. Density is sup over s in S and t>=s of integral_{E intersect {N in omega_t}} chi_{I_t}. Size is sup over +trees T subset S of (|I_T|^(-1)sum_{s in T}|<f,phi_s>|^2)^(1/2). A displayed forest has count=sum_T |I_T|.
items.proof_plan: Fix kappa, admissible tops and +tree convention explicitly. Use ancestor supremum in density to control spatial tails; unnormalised chi would introduce the wrong length factor. Count belongs to a specified tree decomposition, not a unique intrinsic decomposition.
